title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a single handwritten sheet. It is apparently misfiled among typed pages of a Bourbaki draft on Lie groups (n° 413), which are unrelated. Its mathematics belongs to the 'Galois theory of motives' project.

Setting: K is a number field and A is (presumably) its ring of integers. M_0 is a category of 'motifs abéliens'. Given what follows, this most plausibly means motives with abelian Galois action and with Hodge/Hodge–Tate type of CM kind; it may also mean motives of CM abelian varieties.

The motivic Galois group G of M_0 is described as the canonical extension 0 → G^0 → G → Γ → 0:
- G^0 is a (pro-)torus.
- Γ = 'Pic(A)^abs', an absolute (profinite, limit-over-moduli) class group. By class field theory this is essentially Gal(K̃/K), where K̃ is 'the absolute class field' (margin), i.e. the maximal abelian extension.

Structurally this is exactly the shape of Serre's groups 0 → T_m → S_m → C_m → 0 (Serre, Abelian l-adic representations, 1968, built from Taniyama 1957 and Weil's Hecke characters of type A_0). In Grothendieck's notation, C_m is the ray class group 'Pic' and T_m is the torus.

Next, every place ξ of K gives a fibre functor ('fibre en ξ'), i.e. a Betti-type realization. It identifies M_0 (equivalently) with Rep_Q(G), finite-dimensional Q-vector spaces with G-action. The Hodge realization at ξ factors through this, giving a canonical functor Φ_ξ: Rep_Q(G) → Q-Hodge structures, with a real structure (an F_∞-type involution) when ξ is real.

In modern terms, Φ_ξ amounts to a homomorphism h_ξ: S = Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R, landing in G^0_R. It is determined by the canonical cocharacter of the Serre torus, conjugated according to the place.

The last paragraph says that to build Φ_ξ it suffices to have two pieces of data:
- the action of the multiplicative group of K (as an algebraic group) on V coming from the G^0-action (the weight/CM-type grading by characters of the torus);
- a family of structures indexed by places ξ of K̃ which 'contain' the Hodge structures.

This is the Hodge datum that later appears in the Taniyama group: the Hodge cocharacters attached to the different embeddings, permuted by Galois. In short, the page sketches the motivic Galois group of abelian/CM motives over K as an extension of Gal(K^ab/K) by a torus, together with the Hodge realizations at all places.
errors: Purely schematic: G^0 is not specified, nor is it shown that the fibre functor is an equivalence. The claim that M_0 is neutral Tannakian with this group is asserted, not proved.
Rep_Q(G) for an extension of a profinite Γ by a torus requires interpreting G as a pro-algebraic Q-group scheme (Γ as a pro-finite constant/étale group). This is not addressed.

Using a single place ξ of K for a Betti fibre functor requires an embedding of K into C (a place of K̃ or K̄, not of K). The text itself shifts to 'ξ de K̃' at the end, showing the indexing is not yet settled.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group of abelian (CM-type) motives over K is an extension of the abelianized Galois group / absolute class group by a pro-torus
ideas.modern_name: Serre group S_K, S_m (Serre 1968); motivic Galois group of CM motives; Taniyama group (Langlands 1979, Deligne 1982)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1968) for S_m; Langlands and Deligne (Motifs et groupes de Taniyama, LNM 900, 1982); Milne–Shih
ideas.where_published: Only the general idea of a motivic Galois group appears via Grothendieck's letters and Saavedra's thesis (1972); this specific extension is not known to be in his texts (unsure)

ideas.what: Tannakian equivalence M_0 ≃ Rep_Q(G) via the fibre functor at a place
ideas.modern_name: Neutral Tannakian category with Betti fibre functor
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (from Grothendieck's ideas)

ideas.what: Canonical functors Φ_ξ: Rep(G) → Hodge structures (+ real structure at real places), indexed by places, obtained from the torus action plus a family of place-indexed structures
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter μ of the Serre torus and its Galois conjugates; Hodge realization of CM motives / Taniyama group datum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Hodge type of S), Deligne (1979–82), Langlands (1979)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, in the motivic/Tannakian language, the motivic Galois group of abelian motives over a number field. He gives it as an extension of the absolute class group (Gal(K^ab/K)) by a torus, equipped with Hodge realizations indexed by places of K^ab. This anticipates the Serre-group / Taniyama-group picture, which the literature credits to Serre (1968), Langlands (1979) and Deligne (1982), without reference to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Extension canonique de Γ par le tore G^0, 0 → G^0 → G → Γ → 0, Γ = Pic(A)^abs ... toute place ξ de K définit un morphisme de foncteurs ... d'où un foncteur canonique Vectoriels sur Q avec op. de G → vectoriels de Hodge
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If the sheet really dates from 1965 (the cote spans 1965–c.1977), it is a documentary trace that Grothendieck had the Tannakian interpretation of Serre/Taniyama-type groups as motivic Galois groups of CM/abelian motives. That would predate its usual attribution. This is relevant to the history of the Taniyama group and of motivic Galois groups.

missed.claim: The idea that Φ_ξ is determined by the torus (weight/CM-type) action plus a family of structures indexed by places of K̃ is left unarticulated. It is essentially the problem of describing how the Hodge realizations at different embeddings are related (Deligne's conjugation of CM motives / the Taniyama group's role).
missed.quote: + une famille de structures de ξ de K̃, qui en contiennent les structures de Hodge
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than new mathematics. The later theory (Deligne, Milne–Shih, Langlands) completes it.

deep.surprise_reason: A compact sketch of an extension of Gal(K^ab/K) by a torus serving as the motivic Galois group of abelian motives, with place-indexed Hodge realizations, in the Taniyama/Serre-group spirit. If dated 1965 it predates Serre's book and the Taniyama group. However, it is only a sketch, its date is uncertain within 1965–1977, and Serre's S_m were already in the air (Taniyama, Weil). So it is a notable historical detail, not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The first line, rendered as 'C'est-à-dire[?]', is an uncertain heading (possibly 'Ci-dessus' or similar); it is circled with an arc linking to the inserted words 'le tore'.
Under M_0 the '||' links to 'motifs abéliens'; the '~' under the arrow, with 'équiv.', indicates the fibre functor is an equivalence.

Last paragraph: 'Il est clair d'ailleurs d'avoir' is more likely 'Il suffit d'ailleurs d'avoir les opérations de K^* sur V (venant de G^0 sur V, i.e. le K^* sur V venant de l'action triviale de E), + une famille de structures, ...'.
Margin note: 'K̃ = corps de classes absolu' (the maximal abelian extension).
